sources.title: MiniMax Code Preview launch announcement
sources.evidence: Official MiniMax Code account announces M3.1-Flash-Preview debut for coding on September 27, 2026. Direct X page returned 403; public X syndication JSON supplied exact post, official organization affiliation and created_at 2026-09-27T05:24:55Z.

sources.title: MiniMax Preview Token Plan announcement
sources.evidence: Official MiniMax account announces availability on Token Plan on September 27 at 17:06:37Z. Retrieved directly through public X syndication JSON; quotes the earlier MiniMax Code announcement.

sources.title: Archived MiniMax M3.1-Flash-Preview product guide, October 11
sources.evidence: Complete archived original developer page, canonical URL identifies the Preview. FAQ explicitly gives 428B total, about 23B active, MoE, sparse attention and a native visual encoder. Exact Preview comparison lists 1,000,000 context, text/image/video inputs and text output. The live URL now redirects to the GA successor.

sources.title: Archived MiniMax model invocation documentation, October 1
sources.evidence: Exact Preview ID is available only through M Plan and MiniMax Code. Documents 1,000,000 context, agentic reasoning, tool use, coding and multimedia input; reasoning is mandatory with five adjustable effort levels. Includes exact-ID OpenAI and Anthropic examples.

sources.title: Archived MiniMax Anthropic compatibility documentation, October 10
sources.evidence: Exact Preview is in supported-model table; tool definitions, tool_choice, tool_use and tool_result blocks are supported. Text/image/video inputs are explicit. Reasoning cannot be disabled and effort supports low, medium, high, xhigh and max.

sources.title: Official MiniMax M3.1 public repository listing
sources.evidence: Current official-organization query returns the final MiniMax-M3.1-Flash repository only. Direct exact Preview and preview-private API requests return 401; that response alone does not establish whether a private repository exists. No publicly accessible exact Preview weights were verified.

sources.title: Later MiniMax M3.1 Flash release card
sources.evidence: Later final-release card was checked for retrospective disclosure. It reports 428B/23B and MoE for final Flash, with no Preview comparison or checkpoint-identity assertion. Its weights and Community License are not transferred to Preview.

sources.title: Current MiniMax M3.1 Flash product page
sources.evidence: FAQ calls the GA model the successor to M3.1-Flash-Preview. The old Preview URL now redirects here; this does not establish identical checkpoints.

sources.title: MiniMax Sparse Attention technical report
sources.evidence: Primary attention report linked by later Flash card describes 109B experimental models and links production M3. It does not label Preview architecture dimensions or counts; none are transferred.

name.note: Exact historical API identifier, distinct from final MiniMax-M3.1-Flash.

developer.note: Official developer announcements and archived developer product page.

family.note: The exact Preview is described as an M-series language model; retains catalog family key.

release_date.note: Direct official post timestamps establish initial named Preview availability, before the October 19 final release. Anonymous Space Bunny is not assumed to be the identical checkpoint.

open_weights.note: Preview was distributed through hosted products. No public exact-Preview checkpoint was found; later released final weights do not establish Preview weight availability.

license.note: Descriptive classification for the hosted Preview with no public redistributable weight license. The final Flash Community License is not assigned to this earlier variant.

parameters_b.note: Nominal developer figure specifically naming Preview in the archived product FAQ. This is not a checkpoint census; component boundaries are unspecified.

active_parameters_b.note: Approximate developer active count for the exact Preview. The source does not define per-component or phase accounting; no precise tensor-derived interpretation is asserted.

architecture.note: The exact Preview FAQ names MoE, sparse attention and a native vision encoder. No layer/expert dimensions or final-release DSpark implementation are inferred.

context_window.note: Historical first-party exact-Preview context limit. This is maximum documented context, not evidence of present endpoint availability or a client default.

modalities.note: Native visual input is explicitly documented for Preview; generated images or video through external tools are not model output modalities.

reasoning.note: Always enabled; exact Preview supports low, medium, high, xhigh and max effort and rejects disabled reasoning.

tool_call.note: Exact-model API compatibility page supports tool definitions and structured tool-use/result blocks, establishing native function calling beyond product-level agent features.

description.value: Preview multimodal MoE model for coding and tool use, with a 1M-token context window and adjustable reasoning effort.
description.note: Replaces promotional frontier wording with exact Preview architecture and documented features.

patch.description: Preview multimodal MoE model for coding and tool use, with a 1M-token context window and adjustable reasoning effort.
patch.notes: Preview-specific nominal 428B total and about 23B active are documented in the archived October 11 developer product FAQ; component counting conventions are unspecified. September 27 launch and 1,000,000 context are primary-sourced. This historical hosted Preview is distinct from the later released Flash checkpoint; its final weights, Community License and detailed architecture are not transferred. Archived docs establish last-documented capabilities, not current endpoint operation.

summary: Verified all 14 fields against exact-Preview primary evidence, including archived developer pages. Adds nominal 428B total, about 23B active, MoE architecture and hosted proprietary classification. Confirms September 27 release, 1M context, multimodal input, mandatory reasoning and native tool calling. Does not transfer final Flash weight availability or license; no exact Preview checkpoint was public in the reviewed sources.
